entities.summary:
Kashtiliash II was the king of the Elamites from approximately 1595 to 1551 BCE, playing a crucial role in the politics of the Ancient Near East during the Late Bronze Age. He was a key figure in the conflict between the Elamites and the Mitanni Empire.


  Kashtiliash II is also known for his diplomatic relations with the Egyptians, who were a major power in the region at the time. The Egyptian pharaoh, Horemheb, sent a delegation to Elam, which led to a peace treaty between the two nations.


  The reign of Kashtiliash II also saw significant economic growth in Elam, as the country became a major producer of copper and other metals. This economic prosperity helped to establish Elam as a major power in the region.


  Kashtiliash II's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his diplomatic efforts helped to establish a lasting peace between Elam and Egypt, and his economic policies contributed to the growth of the Elamite civilization.


  The fact that Kashtiliash II was able to negotiate a peace treaty with Egypt is a testament to his skill as a diplomat, and his ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries that existed in the Ancient Near East.
